data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental in April means enjoying mild weather, calm seas, and the festive buzz of Easter. With average temperatures of 18°C and up to 12 hours of sunshine, it's one of the best months for a charter before the summer crowds arrive. Whether you're after a sunset cruise from Puerto Banús or a day trip to Estepona, this guide covers everything you need—weather, sea conditions, boat options, and insider tips.

April Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

April brings spring to the Costa del Sol. Daytime highs reach 22°C, dropping to 12°C in the evening. Sea temperature sits at 16°C—cool but refreshing. Rain is infrequent: about 4-5 days of light showers, usually short-lived. Sunshine hours increase from 8 early in the month to 12 by Easter. The Marbella boat rental season kicks off properly in April, with fewer crowds than summer.

Sea Conditions for Boating in April

The Mediterranean off Marbella is calm in April. Wave heights average 0.3-0.8m, with light easterly winds of 5-10 knots. The coastline from Marbella to Sotogrande is sheltered, making for smooth sailing. Occasionally, a levante wind can stir up chop, but our skippers adjust routes to calmer spots like Cala del Faro or Cabopino. Visibility underwater is good for snorkelling near rocky coves.

Best Boats for an April Charter

For small groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax, €749/2h) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax, same price) are perfect. Both include a skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719/4h) comes with a free jet ski. All depart from Puerto Banús. Other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Pershing 46 are available on request via WhatsApp.

Easter Week: Tips for a Smooth Rental

Easter week is peak season for April charters. Book 2-3 weeks ahead to secure your preferred boat. Morning slots (10:00-14:00) are quieter than afternoons. Puerto Banús gets busy, but sea traffic remains moderate. Sunset cruises are popular—golden hour around 20:30. Our fleet of 16 boats ensures flexibility, from the speedy Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) to the spacious Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax).

Where to Go on an April Boat Trip

Popular routes include heading west to Estepona (15 NM) or east to Cabopino (10 NM). Anchor at Cala Cortés for a quiet swim stop. For dining, try a lunch at a chiringuito in Sotogrande. The Golden Mile coastline offers views of La Concha mountain. Our skippers know the best spots for dolphin sightings near Cala del Faro. All trips include complimentary drinks and snacks on board.

What to Wear and Bring

Layers are essential: a light jumper or jacket over a T-shirt. Sunscreen (SPF 30+) is a must even on cloudy days. Non-slip shoes, sunglasses, and a hat help. By midday, you may shed layers as temps hit 22°C. Evenings cool to 12°C, so bring a windbreaker. Towels are not provided, but you can bring your own. The onboard bar stocks water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava.
